programme: NKRF and HDAC1 form the corepressor pairing documented at NF-κB target genes (NKRF recruits HDAC1 to shut down IL-8/CXCL8, iNOS/NOS2 and COX2/PTGS2 transcription after the initial NF-κB pulse), and NPAS2, as a core circadian transcription factor, sets the timing of this repressive tone rather than being a physical member of the complex.
role_in_a: In Alzheimer's disease, HDAC1 is placed at the blood-brain barrier (ZNF787/HDAC1 regulating BBB permeability) and downstream of short-chain-fatty-acid signalling onto Tau phosphorylation; NKRF turns up in a transcriptomic meta-analysis of AD-associated NF-κB pathway regulation; NPAS2 is tied to the astrocyte circadian clock controlling Chi3l1/YKL-40 and neuroinflammatory tone, and to a clock-modulator (nobiletin) affecting AD pathophysiology in mice. Together these place a circadian-gated NF-κB repression axis at the glial/BBB interface.
role_in_b: In IBS, the same three factors are independently placed at the gut barrier: HDAC1 is the target of a compound (cinnamaldehyde) tested in an IBS network-pharmacology/rat model; NKRF is linked to NLRP3-inflammasome-driven inflammation in an IBS-D mouse model and, more directly, to intestinal permeability itself — miR-29 targets NKRF and Claudin-1 to increase gut leakiness; NPAS2 appears via glucocorticoid-receptor/Nr1d1 circadian misalignment in stress-induced IBS. This is the same repression-plus-clock module, applied to epithelial barrier and visceral inflammatory tone instead of the BBB.
shared_axis: A circadian-gated NF-κB corepressor axis — NPAS2 setting the rhythmic window, NKRF and HDAC1 executing repression of cytokine/barrier-relevant genes — could run in both glia/BBB and gut epithelium, so that chronic disruption of clock-gated repression would produce parallel barrier leakiness and inflammatory dysregulation in brain and gut without requiring any AD-specific or IBS-specific cause.
reasoning: The record independently places all three carrying factors in on-point primary literature for both diseases (not reviews or off-topic hits), and the NKRF-HDAC1 pairing is a documented mechanistic unit, not an assumption — the two factors share a direct target (CXCL8) in this network's own target lists, matching the literature's IL-8-repression story. No source states that AD and IBS share this axis, so the cross-disease link itself is inferential, keeping the verdict at 'supported' rather than 'established'.
support: PMID 38738952 (NKRF, meta-analysis/transcriptomics implicating NKRF in AD NF-κB regulation); PMID 36590561 (NKRF-adjacent NLRP3 inflammasome pathway targeted in an IBS-D mouse model); PMID 25277410 (miR-29 targets NKRF and Claudin-1, directly raising intestinal permeability — mechanistic IBS evidence); PMID 38329647 (HDAC1 regulates blood-brain barrier permeability in an AD in vitro model); PMID 40812734 (HDAC1 pathway implicated in SCFA-mediated reduction of Tau hyperphosphorylation, AD); PMID 42500261 (HDAC1 targeted by cinnamaldehyde in an IBS network-pharmacology/rat study); PMID 33328329 (NPAS2/astrocyte circadian clock controls Chi3l1-YKL-40 and neuroinflammation, AD); PMID 34356628 (clock modulator nobiletin affects circadian rhythms and AD pathophysiology in mice); PMID 37404374 (NPAS2-linked Nr1d1 circadian misalignment in stress-induced IBS).
how_to_falsify: In matched glial/BBB and intestinal epithelial cell models, knock down NKRF or HDAC1 and measure whether CXCL8/PTGS2/NOS2 repression is lost in both tissue types under NF-κB stimulation; separately, knock down NPAS2 and test whether the circadian rhythmicity of that repression (not just its magnitude) disappears in both models. If HDAC1/NKRF do not co-occupy the same target promoters in AD brain and IBS colonic mucosa by ChIP, or if NPAS2 loss has no effect on the timing of NKRF/HDAC1-mediated repression in either tissue, the shared circadian-corepression axis does not hold.
caveats: Tissue pairing is brain vs colorectal, only 32 patient-group comparisons drawn from 3 independent cohort pairs, so this rests on limited independent replication. Eight of the twelve concordant factors (TFAP4, TRPS1, MECOM, RREB1, SNAI1, SSRP1, HBP1, KLF1, PRRX1) have no on-point literature for either disease or only tangential/uncertain hits and are excluded from the programme rather than forced in — in particular SNAI1's EMT/tight-junction targets (CDH1, CLDN1, CLDN3) look tempting for a gut-barrier story but its only retrieved papers are cancer/eye-disease and unrelated, so it is left out. NR3C1 (glucocorticoid receptor) was removed from this list as tissue-generic even though the cited IBS NPAS2 paper is framed around GR-Nr1d1 crosstalk — the account here rests on NPAS2 alone, not GR. KLF1 is an erythroid lineage factor with no plausible mechanistic role in either brain or gut tissue and its concordance is likely a blood-contamination or technical artifact rather than biology.
